title: Make the edge of curiosity observable
question: Can TurtleBlock AI continuously synthesize one irresistible next question from the whole ecology of the project without turning curiosity into a backlog or letting the machine mistake a suggestion for authority?
why_now: Today's Terraria, tagging, deployment, Build Log, and navigation work made more of the project itself observable. The next possibility is to make the horizon observable too: one living question that appears only after the newest meaningful build is actually committed.
inputs: D1 research objects, CTC mappings, ontology mappings, uncaptured observations, Terraria traces, and auto-build records when available
R2 artifact metadata and evidence objects when available
runtime/environment metadata when useful, never secret values
project documents and research materials available to the active TurtleBlock AI context
Sanders research ontology with source/later-layer provenance
failures, reversals, rejected candidates, and contradictions
possible_possibles: A recurring uncaptured observation suggests a new Terrarium rather than a new feature.
A D1 pattern suggests a regression test nobody explicitly planned.
A Minecraft affordance unexpectedly collides with an old Logo or STEAMHAMLET idea.
A human correction reveals a weakness in the Turtle Charter or provenance model.
A synthetic Turtle disagreement exposes a representation problem worth testing with humans later.
The best next move is an unglamorous refactor that makes a stranger experiment possible.
Something important appears that the current ontology cannot name yet.
constraints: The Next Edge must point forward, never describe already-completed work.
The newest completed work must appear separately as a committed Build Log entry.
Never inspect, publish, or infer secret values from environment configuration.
A machine may propose the Next Edge; it does not gain production authority from doing so.
Publish one primary horizon question at a time while preserving alternate possible possibles as research metadata.
